clue.text: The saying of masses or collects

indicators.note: the saying of a word means we want something that sounds like it when spoken

parts.note: masses, as in great crowds, are hordes

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is reciting the prayers of the Mass, or the short prayers called collects.
explanation.walkthrough: The religious surface (masses, collects as prayers) hides two plain words: crowds and gathers.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect things is to amass and store them, which is what someone doing this verb does.

clue.text: Dance to score in children's game

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
to scotch is an old verb for to score or cut a line

explanation.surface: Children dance to a scoring system in a playground game.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is played by hopping over lines scored on the ground, and 'scotch' is the old word for such a scored line.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground pastime where players jump across numbered squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: It provides lateral control in lone air trip

indicators.note: trip in the sense of stumble, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A solo flight needs something to keep the plane steady sideways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges LONE AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged flap on an aeroplane wing that controls roll, its sideways tilt.

clue.text: The sort of tack one gets on board

definitions.text: The sort of tack one gets on board

parts.words: The sort of tack one gets on board
parts.note: the board is a drawing board and the tack a short nail holding paper, not a sailing manoeuvre aboard ship

explanation.surface: Sailors discuss the kind of tacking manoeuvre used aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tack' and 'on board' suggest sailing; the board is a drawing board.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pin with a broad flat head, used to fix paper to a board.

clue.text: Lying in, black man had no right to avoid being fired

parts.note: lying in bed is being abed

indicators.note: had no says the letter for right is taken out of the word before it

parts.note: an old, now offensive, word for a black man

explanation.surface: A man lying in bed is told he has no right to keep his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had no' takes R out of NEGRO, leaving NEGO. In the Book of Daniel, Abednego was thrown into the fiery furnace with Shadrach and Meshach and came out unburnt. The surface makes 'fired' mean losing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical figure survived Nebuchadnezzar's furnace unscathed, the one man (with two companions) who escaped burning.

clue.text: Close weeds in rural areas

parts.note: boon in the sense of intimate, as in a boon companion
docks are broad-leaved weeds

explanation.surface: Thick weeds grow nearby in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: BOON as close only survives in 'boon companion', a close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal American word for remote backwoods country far from towns.

clue.text: Pack the floor

definitions.meaning: the floor, or as a verb to knock someone to the floor

explanation.surface: Someone loads up the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a full set of playing cards and also a ship's floor, or knocking someone flat.

clue.text: Account for former flat

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a plain is a flat stretch of land

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to explain what happened to their old apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment; it is level ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the reasons for something, to justify or clarify it.

clue.text: The system for counting pieces of eight, presumably

definitions.text: The system for counting pieces of eight, presumably

parts.words: The system for counting pieces of eight, presumably
parts.note: treats pirate coins as if they would naturally be reckoned in a base-eight number system

explanation.surface: A pirate wonders how to count his Spanish dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces of eight were Spanish silver coins; the joke is that they would be counted in base eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A number system built on base eight, using only digits nought to seven.

clue.text: Hand over to heirs utterly

indicators.note: utterly in the sense of when uttered, spoken aloud

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring, a family's heirs

explanation.surface: Someone gives everything to their heirs entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' looks like 'completely' but means 'when spoken'.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield or surrender a right or territory to another party.

clue.text: Large amount, including money and silver, in sack

indicators.note: including says one piece holds the following letters inside it

parts.note: a large amount is a pile
L is the abbreviation for pound, so for money
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A big haul of cash and silver is stuffed into a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like the bag holding the loot, but it is the definition, the verb meaning to plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, the same as looting and ransacking.

clue.text: Old, small volume I had to deposit — the head's back!

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, measures a small volume
to deposit something is to put it down

explanation.surface: Someone had to put an old little book down and exclaims about the back of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: This anatomical term names the rear part of the skull.

clue.text: Things that must be put right in bullfighting — the facts

definitions.text: Things that must be put right

indicators.note: in says the facts are placed inside the word for bullfighting

parts.note: a corrida is a Spanish bullfight
gen is British slang for information, the facts

explanation.surface: A writer wants the bullfighting facts straightened out.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British informal for information. 'in' puts GEN inside CORRIDA after its fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin plural names errors listed for correction in a printed book, so items needing amendment.

clue.text: Fixative to stop the teeth moving

definitions.text: Fixative to stop the teeth moving

parts.words: Fixative to stop the teeth moving
parts.note: sounds like dental glue, but describes a pivoted catch that locks into a ratchet's cogs

explanation.surface: A dental adhesive keeps loose teeth in place.
explanation.walkthrough: The teeth are a ratchet wheel's cogs, not a mouth's.
explanation.definitionFit: This mechanical catch drops between ratchet cogs so the wheel turns one way only.

clue.text: Mole's holiday on the river

indicators.note: in a down answer, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
a river is a body of water

explanation.surface: A small burrowing animal takes a vacation by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' is not the animal but a harbour wall; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a stone pier or barrier protecting a harbour from waves.

clue.text: Represent a great new American songster

indicators.note: to represent the letters is to present them again, rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh American singer performs a great song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represent' rearranges A GREAT plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: This colourful songbird lives in the Americas, so a songster in the bird sense.

clue.text: Deplored rude noise

definitions.meaning: the sound of the word rude is rued, which means felt sorry about

explanation.surface: Someone disapproved of a vulgar sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude noise' means the word 'rude' spoken, which sounds like 'rued'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplore something or to have rued it both mean feeling sorry about it.

clue.text: Confirmed account after the French left

indicators.note: left in the sense of gone away, so the French article is dropped

parts.note: a chronicle is an account of events
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An account was confirmed after the French side departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes LE from the end of CHRONICLE. 'Confirmed' is meant in the sense of habitual, as in a confirmed bachelor.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual, long-standing condition or habit is described as persistent and incurable, the medical sense.

clue.text: In a position to win match after set-back

indicators.note: after says the word for match follows the word for set-back

parts.note: a check is a setback or halt
to mate is to pair or match

explanation.surface: A player is ready to win the match after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess term is a position in which a king cannot escape, so the game is won.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess this is the winning position, where the opposing king is trapped.

clue.text: Hiring out a horse with a sort of cough

definitions.meaning: a hack is a horse for hire, and letting one out is the business of a livery stable
a dry, harsh, repeated cough has this name

explanation.surface: A stable owner rents out a horse that has a nasty cough.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacks are hired riding horses, and a rasping persistent cough is described with the same word.

clue.text: Confined to two sleeping places

parts.note: a crib is a baby's sleeping place
a bed is a sleeping place

explanation.surface: Someone is restricted to just two beds.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cramped or shut in is to be restricted, kept in a small space.

clue.text: Walk: unsteadily through most of the abattoir

indicators.note: most of says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a shambles is an old word for a slaughterhouse

explanation.surface: Someone totters through a slaughterhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAMBLES, an old word for an abattoir, loses its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: To lurch along with a shuffling, awkward gait is to walk unsteadily.

clue.text: System providing a digital read-out

parts.note: digital means done with the fingers: a script of raised dots read by touch

explanation.surface: A gadget shows its information on an electronic number display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests electronics; it means done with the fingers (digits).
explanation.definitionFit: A tactile script of raised dots that blind people read with their fingertips.

clue.text: He is right to hold on to property in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back means the word is read from end to start

parts.words: right to hold on to property
parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A man looks back and decides he was right to keep his property.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, so a male person referred to as he.

clue.text: Down a dirty section of the pits

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone goes down into a dirty part of the mine.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of anything, informally called the very worst.

clue.text: Bird figuring in field sport

parts.note: a meadow is a grassy field
a lark is a bit of fun or sport

explanation.surface: A bird turns up in a country sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American songbird of open grassland.

clue.text: St Paul's has one in the same state

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same
ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: St Paul's Cathedral has something in the same condition as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the same state' reads as unchanged condition; it splits into ditto and Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul's Cathedral in London is crowned by a great rounded roof, a famous cupola.

clue.text: Distribute notes

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone hands out notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to allot or dole out shares.

clue.text: Where to place daughter with the better set

indicators.note: set in the sense of arranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A family wants its daughter placed among the better class of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges BETTER into EBRETT. Debrett's Peerage is the British guide that records the rank and place of the aristocracy, the 'better set' of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This reference book lists the titled families and how they rank, so it is where one finds a person's social standing.

clue.text: Waltzer laid out on the rug

indicators.note: on says the rearranged letters follow the rug

parts.note: a mat is a small rug

indicators.note: out in the sense of disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancer lies sprawled on the rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns LAID into ILDA, written after MAT. The song Waltzing Matilda, the unofficial Australian anthem, gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian bush song names the swag a traveller carries, which goes waltzing along with him.

clue.text: They were in league, according to Holmes

definitions.text: They were in league, according to Holmes

parts.words: They were in league, according to Holmes
parts.note: points to a Conan Doyle story about a club open only to men with hair of a certain colour

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes accuses some people of conspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In league' sounds like conspiracy; it refers to The Red-Headed League, a Sherlock Holmes story.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional league in the Holmes story admitted only ginger-haired men.

clue.text: Stand stock still and get very cold

definitions.meaning: to become chilled to the point of ice

explanation.surface: Someone stands motionless outdoors and gets chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both halting all motion and turning to ice.
